claims.text: Conventionally cast MnFe(P,Si)-based alloy has a coarse and heterogeneous microstructure.
Conventionally cast MnFe(P,Si)-based alloy contains compositional gradients and inherent defects.
Spark plasma sintering will refine the microstructure of MnFe(P,Si)-based alloy relative to conventional casting.
Spark plasma sintering will make the MnFe(P,Si)-based alloy microstructure more homogeneous.
Spark plasma sintering will produce fine grains in the MnFe(P,Si)-based alloy.
Spark plasma sintering will minimize porosity and internal defects in the MnFe(P,Si)-based alloy.
Compositional gradients and defects hinder cooperative magnetic ordering in MnFe(P,Si)-based alloys.
Reducing compositional gradients and defects will sharpen the magneto-structural transition.
A sharper magneto-structural transition will enhance the magnetocaloric response.
SPS-processed MnFe(P,Si)-based alloy will exhibit a higher adiabatic temperature change than conventionally cast material.
SPS processing will reduce the critical magnetic field needed to trigger the magneto-structural transition.
Improvement in magnetocaloric performance depends on optimization of the SPS processing parameters.
Deleterious phases induced during SPS could offset the benefits of microstructural refinement.
The proposed benefit may be limited to material systems with strongly coupled magnetic and structural transitions.
